metadata.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
metadata.authors: John Schulman, Filip Wolski, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alec Radford, Oleg Klimov

nodes.name: Policy Gradient Estimator
nodes.statement: The policy gradient estimator $\hat{g} = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)\, \hat{A}_t]$, where $\pi_\theta$ is a stochastic policy and $\hat{A}_t$ is an estimator of the advantage function at timestep $t$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard policy gradient estimator using log-policy times advantage.

nodes.name: Vanilla Policy Gradient Surrogate Loss $L^{PG}$
nodes.statement: $L^{PG}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)\, \hat{A}_t]$ — the loss whose gradient yields the policy gradient estimator $\hat{g}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Loss whose gradient is the policy gradient estimator.

nodes.name: Probability Ratio $r_t(\theta)$
nodes.statement: $r_t(\theta) = \dfrac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid s_t)}$, so $r_t(\theta_{\text{old}}) = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Ratio of current to old policy probabilities at $(s_t,a_t)$.

nodes.name: Conservative Policy Iteration Surrogate $L^{CPI}$
nodes.statement: $L^{CPI}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\!\left[\dfrac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid s_t)} \hat{A}_t\right] = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[r_t(\theta) \hat{A}_t]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Importance-sampled surrogate from conservative policy iteration.

nodes.name: Clipped Surrogate Objective $L^{CLIP}$
nodes.statement: $L^{CLIP}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\big[\min(r_t(\theta) \hat{A}_t,\ \mathrm{clip}(r_t(\theta), 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon) \hat{A}_t)\big]$, where $\epsilon$ is a hyperparameter (e.g.\ $\epsilon = 0.2$).
nodes.statement_clean: PPO clipped objective taking the minimum of unclipped and clipped probability-ratio surrogates.

nodes.name: KL-Penalized Surrogate $L^{KLPEN}$
nodes.statement: $L^{KLPEN}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\!\left[\dfrac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid s_t)} \hat{A}_t - \beta\, \mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\cdot \mid s_t),\, \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid s_t)]\right]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Surrogate objective penalized by KL divergence between old and new policies.

nodes.name: Truncated Generalized Advantage Estimator (GAE)
nodes.statement: $\hat{A}_t = \delta_t + (\gamma\lambda)\delta_{t+1} + \cdots + (\gamma\lambda)^{T-t+1}\delta_{T-1}$, where $\delta_t = r_t + \gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Truncated GAE advantage estimator over a $T$-step trajectory segment.

nodes.name: Combined PPO Objective with Value Function and Entropy Bonus
nodes.statement: $L_t^{CLIP+VF+S}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\!\left[L_t^{CLIP}(\theta) - c_1 L_t^{VF}(\theta) + c_2 S[\pi_\theta](s_t)\right]$, where $L_t^{VF} = (V_\theta(s_t) - V_t^{\text{targ}})^2$ and $S$ is an entropy bonus.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint PPO loss combining clipped surrogate, value-function squared error, and entropy bonus.

nodes.name: TRPO Constrained Surrogate Maximization
nodes.statement: Maximize $\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\!\left[\dfrac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid s_t)}\hat{A}_t\right]$ subject to $\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\cdot \mid s_t), \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid s_t)]] \leq \delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: TRPO problem: maximize surrogate objective under a KL trust-region constraint.
conclusions: Updated $\theta$ that maximizes surrogate within KL ball of radius $\delta$

nodes.name: TRPO Penalized Surrogate Optimization
nodes.statement: Solve the unconstrained problem $\max_\theta \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\!\left[\dfrac{\pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t \mid s_t)}\hat{A}_t - \beta\, \mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\cdot \mid s_t), \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid s_t)]\right]$ for some coefficient $\beta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Penalized variant of TRPO with KL divergence as a soft penalty.

nodes.name: Truncated $n$-step Advantage Estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{A}_t = -V(s_t) + r_t + \gamma r_{t+1} + \cdots + \gamma^{T-t+1} r_{T-1} + \gamma^{T-t} V(s_T)$, the estimator used in the $T$-step actor style of [Mni+16].
nodes.statement_clean: Truncated finite-horizon advantage estimator (recovers Eq.~(11) at $\lambda=1$).

nodes.name: Adaptive KL Penalty Coefficient
nodes.statement: Per-update procedure: optimize $L^{KLPEN}$ with several epochs of minibatch SGD, then adapt $\beta$ based on the measured KL divergence relative to a target $d_{\text{targ}}$.
output: Updated penalty coefficient $\beta$ for next iteration
nodes.pseudocode: Optimize $L^{KLPEN}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[r_t(\theta)\hat{A}_t - \beta \mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}, \pi_\theta]]$ for several epochs of minibatch SGD; compute $d = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\cdot|s_t), \pi_\theta(\cdot|s_t)]]$; if $d < d_{\text{targ}}/1.5$ then $\beta \leftarrow \beta/2$; if $d > 1.5\, d_{\text{targ}}$ then $\beta \leftarrow 2\beta$.

nodes.name: PPO, Actor-Critic Style (Algorithm 1)
nodes.statement: PPO with fixed-length trajectory segments: each iteration $N$ parallel actors collect $T$ timesteps, advantages are estimated, and the surrogate $L$ is optimized for $K$ epochs of minibatch SGD/Adam over $NT$ samples.
nodes.pseudocode: for iteration = 1, 2, \ldots do: for actor = 1, \ldots, N do: run policy $\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}$ for $T$ timesteps; compute advantage estimates $\hat{A}_1, \ldots, \hat{A}_T$; end for; optimize surrogate $L$ wrt $\theta$ with $K$ epochs and minibatch size $M \leq NT$; $\theta_{\text{old}} \leftarrow \theta$; end for.

nodes.name: TRPO (Conjugate-Gradient Surrogate Maximization)
nodes.statement: Solves the TRPO constrained surrogate problem by linearizing the objective and quadratically approximating the KL constraint, then applying the conjugate-gradient method.
output: Updated parameters $\theta$ approximately solving the trust-region problem

nodes.name: Multiple Updates on $L^{PG}$ are Unjustified
nodes.statement: While appealing, performing multiple steps of optimization on $L^{PG}$ using the same trajectory is not well-justified and empirically often leads to destructively large policy updates.

nodes.name: $L^{CLIP}$ is a Pessimistic Lower Bound on $L^{CPI}$
nodes.statement: Taking the minimum of clipped and unclipped surrogates makes $L^{CLIP}$ a lower bound (pessimistic bound) on $L^{CPI}$; the change in probability ratio is ignored when it would improve the objective and included when it makes it worse.

nodes.name: First-Order Equivalence at $\theta_{\text{old}}$
nodes.statement: $L^{CLIP}(\theta) = L^{CPI}(\theta)$ to first order around $\theta_{\text{old}}$ (i.e.\ where $r = 1$); they diverge as $\theta$ moves away from $\theta_{\text{old}}$.

nodes.name: Difficulty of Choosing Fixed Penalty $\beta$
nodes.statement: TRPO uses a hard constraint rather than a penalty because no single value of $\beta$ performs well across (or even within) different problems; experiments confirm a fixed $\beta$ is insufficient for a first-order TRPO emulator.

nodes.name: Single-Timestep Plot of $L^{CLIP}$ (Figure 1)
nodes.statement: Figure 1 plots a single term of $L^{CLIP}$ as a function of $r$ for positive and negative advantages, illustrating that $r$ is clipped at $1-\epsilon$ or $1+\epsilon$ depending on the sign of $\hat{A}_t$.

nodes.name: Surrogate Interpolation on Hopper-v1 (Figure 2)
nodes.statement: Figure 2 shows several objectives ($\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\mathrm{KL}_t]$, $L^{CPI}$, the clipped expectation, and $L^{CLIP}$) along the policy update direction obtained by PPO on Hopper-v1, demonstrating that $L^{CLIP}$ is a lower bound on $L^{CPI}$ with a penalty for too-large updates.

nodes.name: Surrogate Objective Comparison on 7 MuJoCo Tasks (Table 1)
nodes.statement: Compared no-clipping/no-penalty, clipping with $\epsilon \in \{0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$, fixed KL with $\beta \in \{0.3, 1, 3, 10\}$, and adaptive KL with $d_{\text{targ}} \in \{0.003, 0.01, 0.03\}$ on 7 OpenAI Gym MuJoCo tasks; clipping with $\epsilon = 0.2$ achieved the best average normalized score (0.82).

nodes.name: Continuous Control Comparison (Figure 3)
nodes.statement: PPO (clipped, $\epsilon = 0.2$) compared to TRPO, CEM, vanilla PG with adaptive stepsize, A2C, and A2C+Trust Region on 7 MuJoCo tasks (HalfCheetah, Hopper, InvertedDoublePendulum, InvertedPendulum, Reacher, Swimmer, Walker2d); PPO outperforms previous methods on almost all environments.

nodes.name: 3D Humanoid Roboschool Showcase
nodes.statement: PPO trained on RoboschoolHumanoid (forward locomotion), RoboschoolHumanoidFlagrun (target position randomized every 200 timesteps), and RoboschoolHumanoidFlagrunHarder (robot pelted by cubes, must get up off the ground); learning curves in Figure 4, hyperparameters in Table 4.

nodes.name: Atari ALE Comparison (Table 2, 49 games)
nodes.statement: PPO compared with A2C and ACER on 49 Arcade Learning Environment games. PPO wins 30/49 by avg.\ episode reward over training (vs.\ ACER 18, A2C 1) and 19/49 by avg.\ over the last 100 episodes (vs.\ ACER 28, A2C 1).

nodes.name: Justification that $L^{CLIP}$ is a pessimistic lower bound
nodes.statement: Argues that taking the elementwise minimum of $r_t \hat{A}_t$ and $\mathrm{clip}(r_t, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon)\hat{A}_t$ produces an objective that is below the unclipped surrogate, by considering the sign of $\hat{A}_t$ and which term is smaller.

nodes.name: Optimize $L^{KLPEN}$ with several epochs of minibatch SGD
nodes.statement: Run several epochs of minibatch SGD on $L^{KLPEN}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[r_t(\theta)\hat{A}_t - \beta\, \mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}, \pi_\theta]]$ to update $\theta$.

nodes.name: Compute mean KL divergence $d$
nodes.statement: Compute $d = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\mathrm{KL}[\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\cdot \mid s_t), \pi_\theta(\cdot \mid s_t)]]$ over the sampled batch.

nodes.name: Adjust $\beta$ based on $d$ vs.\ $d_{\text{targ}}$
nodes.statement: If $d < d_{\text{targ}}/1.5$, set $\beta \leftarrow \beta/2$; if $d > 1.5\, d_{\text{targ}}$, set $\beta \leftarrow 2\beta$. Otherwise leave $\beta$ unchanged.

nodes.name: Outer iteration loop
nodes.statement: for iteration = $1, 2, \ldots$ do: execute the inner data-collection and optimization steps below.

nodes.name: Parallel actor data collection
nodes.statement: for actor = $1, \ldots, N$ do: run policy $\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}$ in the environment for $T$ timesteps; compute advantage estimates $\hat{A}_1, \ldots, \hat{A}_T$ (e.g.\ by truncated GAE).

nodes.name: Optimize surrogate for $K$ epochs
nodes.statement: Optimize the surrogate loss $L$ (typically $L^{CLIP}$ or $L^{CLIP+VF+S}$) wrt $\theta$ with $K$ epochs and minibatch size $M \leq NT$, using SGD or Adam.

nodes.name: Update old policy
nodes.statement: $\theta_{\text{old}} \leftarrow \theta$ — copy current parameters into the old policy used for the next iteration's importance ratios.

nodes.name: Case $\hat{A}_t > 0$
nodes.statement: When $\hat{A}_t > 0$, $\min(r_t \hat{A}_t, \mathrm{clip}(r_t,1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\hat{A}_t)$ caps the contribution at $(1+\epsilon)\hat{A}_t$ for $r_t > 1+\epsilon$, removing the incentive to push $r_t$ above $1+\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Case $\hat{A}_t < 0$
nodes.statement: When $\hat{A}_t < 0$, the minimum picks the unclipped term $r_t \hat{A}_t$ for $r_t < 1-\epsilon$ (since it is more negative), so excursions of $r_t$ below $1-\epsilon$ remain penalized; for $r_t > 1+\epsilon$ the clipped term bounds the loss.

nodes.name: Combine cases to conclude lower-bound property
nodes.statement: In both cases the clipped objective is no larger than the unclipped $L^{CPI}$ contribution (a pessimistic bound), and movements of $r_t$ that would improve the objective beyond the clip range are ignored.
